description: I am a Communications and Electronics Engineering student at UTAS Al Musannah, with experience developing AI-assisted websites and applications. I created Oman Climate AI, an interactive platform using NASA POWER data to explore temperature, humidity and rainfall across Oman. My interests include AI, web development, data analysis, visualisation and Earth science. I am participating independently to develop an innovative, data-driven solution to a NASA challenge.
summary:
Oman Earth Intelligence is an interactive web platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to explore long-term environmental changes across Oman.

The platform integrates NASA POWER Earth science data to analyze temperature, relative humidity, and precipitation. Users can explore locations through an interactive map, visualize historical trends, compare environmental conditions between locations, and examine data-supported insights.

The project combines interactive visualizations, bilingual Arabic-English accessibility, NASA data verification, and AI-assisted scientific explanations to make Earth observation data easier to understand.

By transforming complex environmental datasets into accessible visual information, Oman Earth Intelligence supports environmental awareness, scientific exploration, and evidence-based understanding of climate patterns in Oman.
details:
Oman Earth Intelligence is a bilingual, interactive Earth science platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to help users investigate long-term environmental trends across Oman.

The application integrates NASA POWER data, including near-surface air temperature (T2M), relative humidity (RH2M), and precipitation (PRECTOTCORR_SUM). Users can select locations, explore historical measurements, visualise environmental trends through interactive charts, and compare conditions across different locations and time periods.

Key Features:

  • Interactive map of Oman for exploring environmental data.
  • Historical temperature, humidity, and precipitation analysis.
  • Location comparison, including Muscat and Al Buraimi.
  • NASA Data Verification Lab for checking scientific measurements.
  • CSV export for further analysis.
  • AI-assisted scientific explanations based on environmental data.
  • Bilingual Arabic and English interface.

Technology and Data Sources:

The platform was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, MapLibre GL, Three.js, and Cloudflare Workers. NASA POWER provides the environmental measurements, while geographic boundary information is attributed to Oman's National Centre for Statistics and Information (NCSI).

Project Objective:

The project aims to make NASA Earth science data more accessible to students, researchers, and the public. By transforming complex environmental datasets into interactive visualisations and understandable explanations, the platform supports environmental awareness, scientific exploration, and evidence-based understanding of environmental changes across Oman.

Development and Transparency:

The project was developed through iterative engineering, testing, and scientific data verification, with assistance from AI tools including ChatGPT and Codex. External resources, AI-assisted contributions, and any reused prior work must be appropriately disclosed in the submission.
